thread:
ashley: heads up — canary rolled kernel-repack + quant-config v5 at 11:30, seeing a persistent drop in prefix cache hit-rate (was stable ~88% -> ~74%).
ashley: snapshot from the canary metrics: 
```
window=30m total_requests=118k prefix_hits=103k (87.3%) -> 87k (73.7%) after deploy
avg_latency_p50=72ms p95=210ms
```
matt: ouch. any errors in logs?
jin: no obvious errors. but sampling a few traces shows different cache keys for the same user prompt. looks like a canonicalization mismatch.
ashley: exact — keys that used to match now differ by small token sequences at the end (trailing padding / sentinel ordering). example: 
```
old_key: model=gptx-1|ver=20240514|tok_hash=0xabc123|suffix="\u0000"
new_key: model=gptx-1|ver=20240514|tok_hash=0xabc123|suffix=""
```
jin: interesting — kernel-repack changed the attention tiling path, and the quant profile flip removed a trailing null when building KV cache prefix buffers. so fingerprint of the priming buffer changed even though semantic tokens same.
kevin: is this the warmprime fingerprint desync we talked about? (new term?): warmprime = cache keys derived from initial prompt priming sequences; fingerprint desync = identical logical prefix -> different byte-level representation.
ellie: yup. reproducer: run `./perf-client --model gptx-1 --seed prompt.txt --dry-run` and compare `kv_prefix.bin` SHA256 before/after.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary tag=kernel-repack-2024-11 flipped at 1765551200 by @matt
matt: timeline matches. what's the short mitigation? rollback kernel or normalize keys?
ashley: short-term: roll back the kernel-repack on canary to restore hit-rate. medium-term: add canonicalization layer in prefix-key builder to normalize: trim trailing pad tokens, normalize sentinel ordering, and include a model_build_id salt to prevent fragile matches across compile variants.
jin: also want a test in our CI that compares `kv_prefix` bytes across candidate kernel builds for a set of canonical prompts — fail if fingerprint divergence > 0.5% of bytes.
kevin: curious if batching heuristics contribute: different tiling can change per-request token packing, which may reorder prefix serialization when we flatten micro-batches. that could alter keys even without token-level changes.
ellie: confirmed: enabling `batcher.stable_serialize=true` recovers identical keys in local repro. so two levers: serialization deterministic flag + trimming.
matt: action items: 
- ashley rollback-canary (assigned: matt)
- jin add deterministic serialization flag and unit tests (assigned: jin)
- kevin add CI cross-build prefix-fingerprint check (assigned: kevin)
- devops run a small canary with deterministic flag enabled and new kernel to validate (assigned: ellie)

ashley: can we quantify the regressed cost? at 74% hit-rate avg token cost is +18% on canary traffic. if this hits prod at scale would be ~$12k/day delta.
jin: adding normalized-key patch will be a small CPU hit on key build but should pay off in hit-rate and safety across kernel/model swaps.
kevin: let's scope the key-normalizer: 1) strip trailing pad tokens, 2) canonicalize sentinel byte order, 3) include `build_id` namespace so keys don't cross-namespace across incompatible compiles. simple and backward-compatible with migration.
matt: ok let's do rollback and then iterate. thx team. :thumbsup:
ashley: rolling back now, will post follow-up metric ping when canary stabilizes.
